annotations.title: Hot water demand and cylinder size

description:
Work out the daily hot water demand of a dwelling and the size of cylinder a heat
pump needs, using the formula in MIS 3005-D 3.5.2 and the BS 6700 guidance reproduced in MGD 007.

The demand is 45 litres a day for each of N, where N is the greater of the number of bedrooms plus one
and the number of people actually living there. For a new build, where occupancy is unknown, the
bedroom count is used.

The cylinder does not have to hold a whole day's demand, because it reheats as it empties. What it must
cover is the largest draw-off before the heat pump catches up, which is why a larger heat pump needs a
smaller cylinder: reheat time is volume times temperature rise, divided by 14.3 times the kW.

The result gives the BS 6700 minimum, a recommended size rounded to a volume cylinders are made in, and
the reheat time. Note that cylinder volume is not the whole story: a heat pump cylinder needs a much
larger coil than a boiler cylinder, because the water arrives cooler and there is less temperature
difference to drive heat across the surface.

Method from MIS 3005-D. These calculators follow the published MCS methods, for understanding a system and checking a quotation. Anything that gets installed still needs a design and a site survey from a certified installer.

bathrooms.description: Number of bathrooms with a bath. Defaults to 1.

bedrooms.description: Number of bedrooms in the property. Required.

coldWaterTemp.description: Incoming mains temperature in Celsius. Defaults to 10.

heatPumpOutputKw.description: Heat output of the heat pump in kW when it is heating the cylinder. A larger heat pump reheats faster, so it needs less stored volume. Defaults to 6.

occupants.description: Number of people who actually live there, if known. MIS 3005-D takes the greater of this and bedrooms plus one. Leave it out for a new build, where the occupancy is not yet known.

storageTemp.description: Temperature the cylinder is stored at, in Celsius. Defaults to 55, which is a common heat pump setting. A weekly pasteurisation cycle above 60 is separate.

name: hot_water_cylinder

dailyDemandLitres.description: Average daily hot water demand: 45 litres for each of N.

designOccupancy.description: N in the MIS 3005-D formula: the greater of bedrooms plus one and the known occupants.

energyPerDayKwh.description: Heat needed each day to raise the daily demand from mains temperature to storage temperature.

minimumCylinderLitres.description: The BS 6700 minimum for this number of bathrooms and this heat pump output, before the allowance MGD 007 adds for extra bathing capacity.

occupancyBasis.description: Which of the two gave the larger figure.

recommendedCylinderLitres.description: Cylinder volume from the BS 6700 guidance in MGD 007, given the number of baths and the heat pump output.

reheatMinutes.description: Roughly how long the heat pump takes to bring the whole cylinder up from cold, ignoring standing losses.
